title: In this world, every lie you've ever told floats above your head.
formula: Strange act (3 weeks of silence) -> why (the rule + your goal) -> plan, rule taken literally against you (a nod counts) -> big test (her band) -> reversal: the truth raises the number (it counts what's true, and you secretly love the kazoos) -> she wins -> twist ending that loops into the rule
facts: Fiction: no sources needed. Rule: a glowing number above each person's head counts every lie they have ever told, and goes up by one the moment they lie, in words or not.

lines.narration: You haven't said a single word in 3 *weeks*.
lines.spoken: You haven't said a single word in three weeks.
lines.scene: Cold open, busy office: everyone chatting; you at your desk with lips pressed shut and a cartoon zipper drawn across your mouth. Above your head, a huge glowing '4,000'.
lines.camera: Slow push-in between two chatting coworkers to you
lines.gag: A literal zipper across your mouth

lines.narration: Because in this world, every lie you've ever told floats over your head, and yours says *4,000*.
lines.spoken: Because in this world, every lie you've ever told floats over your head, and yours says four thousand.
lines.scene: Street outside: every passer-by has a small glowing number; yours is the biggest thing on the block. A pigeon on a lamp post stares at it.
lines.camera: Crane up from you to the street full of numbers
lines.gag: The pigeon slowly side-eyes your number

lines.narration: Your grandma's at 2. The baby next door is at *11*.
lines.spoken: Your grandma's at two. The baby next door is at eleven.
lines.scene: Two quick inserts: sweet grandma knitting under a '2'; a smug baby in sunglasses under an '11'.
lines.camera: Hard cuts, each with a creep-in
lines.gag: Smug baby in sunglasses

lines.narration: And the girl from the coffee shop is at a perfect *zero*.
lines.scene: Golden morning coffee shop: a barista with a yellow beanie and paint on her sleeves, a soft '0' above her like a halo.
lines.gag: Her 0 glows like a halo; a choir card pops

lines.narration: So you've made a plan: no talking, no lies, no new *numbers*.
lines.scene: Your bedroom wall, night: a hand-drawn plan taped up, three boxes, 'NO TALKING', 'NO LIES', and a crossed-out speech bubble.
lines.gag: Your plan is drawn in crayon

lines.narration: It's going great, until your boss asks if you like his new *haircut*.
lines.scene: Office: your boss leans over your desk, proud of an awful bowl cut with one long strand.
lines.gag: The haircut has a single strand sticking straight up like an antenna

lines.narration: You don't say a word. You just *nod*.
lines.scene: Close-up: your head dips, once.

lines.narration: Ding. 4,001. Turns out a nod *counts*.
lines.spoken: [deadpan] Ding. Four thousand and one. Turns out a nod counts.
lines.scene: Your number rolls from 4,000 to 4,001 like an old scoreboard; the whole office turns to look.
lines.camera: Tilt up to the number, then whip to the staring office
lines.gag: The ding is as loud as a church bell; coffee cups shake

lines.narration: So you stop nodding too. Now you just stand there, like a lamp with *anxiety*.
lines.scene: Montage in one shot: you frozen still at the bus stop, in the lift, at a party, hands at your sides, while people wave at you.
lines.camera: Slow lateral glide past you in three places
lines.gag: Someone hangs their coat on you

lines.narration: But it works. She notices you never brag, never flatter, never fake, and she asks you *out*.
lines.scene: Coffee shop: she slides you a cup with 'DINNER?' written on the sleeve.
lines.camera: Insert on the cup, then push-in on your face
lines.gag: Your face fills red from the chin up

lines.narration: First date, she leans in and asks the one question you've been dreading: "Do you like my *band*?"
lines.scene: Candle-lit restaurant at night. Behind her, a poster on the wall: four people with kazoos, 'THE KAZOO-NAMI, LIVE'.
lines.camera: Over her shoulder to you, then push to the poster
lines.gag: Kazoo band poster

lines.narration: Her band is four people with *kazoos*.
lines.scene: Flash insert: the band on a tiny stage, cheeks puffed, one kazoo blowing out a single sad note card.
lines.gag: A single sad note floats out of a kazoo

lines.narration: The whole restaurant goes quiet. Every head turns to look at your *number*.
lines.scene: Diners, waiters, the chef in the kitchen window all stop and stare up at your 4,001.
lines.camera: Slow orbit around the table as heads turn
lines.gag: Even the lobster in the tank turns to look

lines.narration: One lie, and she'll *see* it.
lines.scene: Close-up on her eyes reflecting your glowing 4,001; behind you, the diners lean in.
lines.gag: Even the lobster in the tank leans against the glass to look

lines.narration: So for the first time in your life, you tell the truth: "It's *terrible*."
lines.spoken: So for the first time in your life, you tell the truth: [flatly] "It's terrible."
lines.scene: You, calm and sincere. Total silence. A cricket card in the corner.
lines.gag: A cricket chirps

lines.narration: *Ding*.
lines.scene: Your number rolls over like an old scoreboard, loud as a church bell.
lines.gag: Every glass in the restaurant rattles

lines.scene: Extreme close-up: 4,002 glowing. Your face drops, ring-eyed shock.
lines.gag: Your eyes go to white rings

lines.narration: You see, that number doesn't count what you say. It counts what's *true*.
lines.scene: The digits of your counter flicker and show a tiny glowing kazoo icon behind them, like an X-ray.
lines.gag: An X-ray of your heart shows a little kazoo inside

lines.narration: And deep down, you *love* those kazoos.
lines.scene: Flash insert: you, alone in your bedroom at night, secretly playing her band's song on a kazoo, eyes closed, swaying.
lines.gag: You're wearing a band T-shirt in the flashback

lines.narration: She looks at your number, then at you, and grins. "You *love* it."
lines.scene: She leans back, triumphant; the diners exhale and go back to eating; tiny heart cards pop between you.
lines.gag: She pulls a kazoo out of her bag and hands it to you

lines.narration: 50 years later, you've been to every one of her shows. Your number says 4,002. Hers says *1*.
lines.spoken: Fifty years later, you've been to every one of her shows. Your number says four thousand and two. Hers says one.
lines.scene: Golden dusk, a tiny stage: old her on kazoo, old you in the front row in a faded band T-shirt. Counters '4,002' and '1'.
lines.gag: You're the only person in the audience, and you're on your feet

lines.narration: She never told you *which* one.
lines.spoken: [whispers] She never told you which one.
lines.scene: Close-up: she winks at camera mid-kazoo. Beside her, you look up at her '1', suspicious.
lines.camera: Push-in on her face, end on the word
lines.gag: Her 1 blinks, guilty
